summary: Refreshed the AI infrastructure and power-bottleneck idea from current Eaton, GE Vernova, and Vertiv results and completed a value-chain-wide public-security screen. The physical demand mechanism remains medium-confidence, but all three researched securities remain baseline-only because current valuation and timing gates fail. Imported Schneider Electric, Quanta Services, and Bloom Energy as identity-only candidates for integrated electrical equipment, interconnection construction, and on-site generation, and created exactly one dependent security-research follow-up for each. No relationship, strategy, signal, allocation, order, or accounting state was created.

evidence.source: PaperTrader current linked-security research and structured assessments
evidence.claim: Eaton, GE Vernova, and Vertiv each have current medium-confidence baseline assessments. Their bounded downside/base-upside pairs are -35.9%/-17.5%, -39.6%/+7.4%, and -38.4%/+4.2%, respectively, so none supports conviction strategy research at its reviewed mark.

Schneider reported that pure data-centre demand accelerated to triple-digit year-over-year growth in the fourth quarter, with uptake across electrical panels, UPS, racks, cooling, and digital offers; this supports a broad equipment hypothesis but not a security conclusion.
Schneider identifies its ordinary shares as SU.PA, ISIN FR0000121972, listed on Euronext Paris; canonical identity was imported as SU.PA/XPAR/EUR/equity.

Quanta identifies PWR common stock on the NYSE and describes transmission, substation, distribution, interconnection, and critical-path data-centre electrical work, while disclosing project-delay, policy, supply-chain, labor, and execution risks.

Bloom identifies BE Class A common stock on the NYSE and on-site fuel-cell exposure to AI data centres; its three largest customers and distributors represented approximately 43%, 13%, and 12% of 2025 revenue, making concentration, financing, fuel, manufacturing, cash, and valuation decisive research gates.
